newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's Petrol to list on Ljubljana bourse.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's Petrol to list on Ljubljana bourse.

text.p: Gasoline trader Petrol, among Slovenia's five biggest companies, will list its shares on the Ljubljana bourse, the stock exchange said on Wednesday.
The company will list 1,676,173 ordinary shares with a nominal value of 6,000 tolars ($38.9) each, representing 80.34 percent of the company's equity.
An exact date for the flotation has not yet been fixed, but Petrol said earlier it expects to list the shares in April.
Petrol expects to pay its first ever dividend of 930 tolars this year, in two instalments. The first payment of 700 tolars should be paid in April and the rest in the last quarter of the year.
The company was privatised in December, but the state still owns a 15.63 percent stake.
Shares of Petrol are currently being traded at around 17,000 tolars on the grey market.
Petrol joins a batch of 32 newly privatised companies that have been listed on the bourse since the beginning of 1996.
Currently there are 26 shares traded on the main market and 34 on the over-the-counter segment of the Ljubljana bourse. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
